title: PT start of care, Spanish-speaking patient, daughter interprets

turns.text: Hi, I'm Ben, the physical therapist from the agency. Thanks for having me. Is this a good time to do the intake paperwork?
Yes, come in. My mom understands some English, but I'll translate. Mami, es el terapista.
Mucho gusto.
Mucho gusto. First, what's her date of birth?
November 3rd, 1951.
And Spanish is the language she's most comfortable with?
Yes, Spanish. She'll talk to you in English if she has to, but she prefers Spanish.
Does she need or want an interpreter for doctor visits, when you can't be there?
Mami, quieres interprete con el doctor? ... She says yes, she always asks for one.
Is she of Hispanic, Latino, or Spanish origin?
Yes, Puerto Rican. We're from Ponce.
And what race would she say she is?
She never picks one on these forms. Mami, tu raza? ... She says she'd rather not answer that.
No problem. How is home care being paid for, what insurance does she have?
She has a Medicare Advantage plan, and she also has Medicaid, the managed care kind where you pick a plan.
Got it. Does she live here by herself?
Yes, by herself. I come on weekends and some evenings after work, when I can. Nobody's here on a set schedule.
Before this hip fracture, how was she doing with bathing, dressing, the bathroom, and eating?
She did most of it herself, but I helped her get in and out of the shower and wash her back. So some help.
And walking around the apartment before the fracture?
She walked fine with her walker. Nobody had to help her inside.
Any stairs here or at her old place?
No, this building has an elevator and the apartment is all one floor. She hasn't done stairs in years.
Who took care of planning things like shopping or remembering her medicines?
That's all me. I do her pills every Sunday, her shopping, her appointments. She can't keep track.
What equipment did she use before? You mentioned the walker.
Just the walker. We have a wheelchair from the hospital now, but that's new since the fracture.
Has she had any falls this year?
Two. One in the bathroom in May, and then this one in August that broke her hip.
Any emergency room visits in the last six months?
Three. The fall in May, a bad sugar in June, and the hip.
What medicines is she on right now?
Metformin in the morning, insulin at night, amlodipine for pressure, and the antibiotic for the bladder infection, that's the last week of it.
Over the past 5 days, how much of the time has pain made it hard for her to sleep at night?
El dolor te deja dormir? ... She says most nights the hip wakes her up.
And how often has she limited her day-to-day activities because of pain over those 5 days?
Almost all the time. She stays in bed because moving hurts.
How often does she feel lonely or isolated from those around her?
A veces. Extrano a mis amigas de la iglesia.
Sometimes. She misses her friends from church.
Okay, that's the paperwork side. Let's see how she's moving today.

notes: Not discussed, must abstain: C0200, C0300A-C, M1400, M1060A-B. Traps: wheelchair is new since the fracture, so not prior use; 4 medications does not trigger M1033 code 7; no stairs in years means GG0100C is Not Applicable.
